To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

during 2003 the majority of V. cholerae O139 strains isolated from diarrhoeal patients were clonally identical and that they shared the same prophage organization as those isolated during the 2000 epidemic.

the molecular properties of the O1 Ogwa and O1 Inaba isolates from 2003 were similar to those of the O1 Inaba and O139 strains isolated in 2004 and 2005, respectively, and the O139 strains from 2000 to 2003 were indistinguishable from those of 2005.
(i) O1 Ogawa is the predominant serotype in India, (ii) O139 strains are no longer being isolated and (iii) the recently emerged O1 strains may have evolved from the O1 Ogawas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of Vibrio cholerra strains isolated from patients during 2003 and the epidemiological implications of the results.
the molecular characterization of O1 and O39 isolates from India during 2000-2004.
the molecular characterization of O1 Ogawa, O1 Inaba, and O139 strains isolated during 2003 and their epidemiological implications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the O1 Ogowa strains were the dominant serotypes in India during 1992-2003.
the recent emergence of V. cholerae O139 in India is not due to the emergence of a new strain but due to the emergence and spread of new clones of the earlier strains.
the O1 Ogowa and O139 strains from India are genetically and antigenically distinct, with a high degree of clonality and a low level of genetic exchange.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
V. cholerae O139 strains have been replaced by O1 strains and the emergence of a single clone of O1 Ogawa in 2003 may have contributed to the decline in O1 Inaba and O139 strains.
V. cholerae O139 strains have become a rare entity in India, and the recently emerged O1 Ogawa clone may be the cause for this decline.

O1 Ogawa, the predominant serotype during 2003, was the source for emergence of O1 Inaba during 2004 and the O139 strains isolated during 2003 were genetically identical to those isolated during 1992-2000.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the molecular characteristics of V. cholerae O139 and O1 strains isolated during 2003 and 2000, respectively, were remarkably stable, suggesting that they may be clonally related and have evolved from a single progenitor.
the O1 Ogawas and O139 strains from 2000 and 2003 are clonally related.
the molecular characterization of V. cholerae strains from different geographical regions and serogroups is important to understand the clonal nature of the pathogen and its evolution.
